ROOT <- "/gpfs1/pi/avolaric/files_jrboyd/P3_CosMx_v2"
## Every read is guarded: a missing intermediate should degrade one block, never kill
## the render. Which files were unavailable is listed in the appendix.
MISSING <- character()
rd <- function(p, ...) {
  f <- file.path(ROOT, p)
  if (!file.exists(f)) { MISSING <<- c(MISSING, p); return(NULL) }
  tryCatch(fread(f, ...), error = function(e) { MISSING <<- c(MISSING, p); NULL })
}
img <- function(p, cap = NULL) {
  f <- file.path(ROOT, p)
  if (!file.exists(f)) { MISSING <<- c(MISSING, p); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  ## rel_path = FALSE: include_graphics otherwise rewrites the path relative to the
  ## Rmd's own directory (scripts/), while the existence check runs from root.dir
  ## (the project root), so "../output/..." resolves outside the project and fails.
  ## self_contained still base64-embeds an absolute path, so portability is kept.
  knitr::include_graphics(f, rel_path = FALSE)
}
tbl <- function(d, cap = NULL, digits = 3) {
  if (is.null(d) || !nrow(d)) return(invisible(NULL))
  kable(d, caption = cap, digits = digits, format = "html",
        table.attr = 'class="table table-sm table-striped"')
}

# Revision notice {-}

<div class="verdict-no">
**This document was revised on 2026-09-01 and supersedes the originally circulated version.**
If you are holding an earlier copy, four findings in it have changed. Everything else is
unaltered. The corrections are made inline below and are also listed here so a reader with the
old version can see what moved without re-reading the whole report.

| what the original said | status now | where it was settled |
|---|---|---|
| Assumption "RB1 is a valid negative control **PRE-QC**" — **FAILED** | **RESOLVED.** The symmetric `matched` QC tier gives IB1 80 chemokine hotspots (66 seam-free) and **zero** RB1 bins clearing the same cut. | step 16, `output/16_summary/step16_FL_comparison.html` |
| CD30 rejected partly because "depth predicts CD30 positivity at **AUC 0.716**" | **THAT LEG IS WITHDRAWN.** AUC ≈ 0.70 against depth is generic to every sparse gene on this platform (*IGKC* 0.693, *CD3E* 0.695, *CD68* 0.731), so it is not evidence about CD30. **The conclusion is unchanged** — see the corrected box in §5.2. | step 16 negprobe/AUC calibration |
| The Hodgkin chemokine field is "**tissue-wide**" | **QUANTIFIED, and the word was imprecise.** The field decays **2.71× [1.95, 3.91]** from 100–400 µm to >1600 µm from a hotspot, against **1.20×** in RB1 (ratio **2.27× [1.62, 3.25]**). Most of it is spent by 400–800 µm; beyond that a flat **4.07×** IB1:RB1 residual remains that is *not* a decaying field and is unattributed. | step 17, `field_extent_verdict.csv` |
| FL-like foci are not transcriptionally distinguishable — attributed to low power, "on n = 6 foci" | **SAME VERDICT, STRONGER CAUSE.** Conditioning on cell type gives **zero** significant genes within B or T cells. The FL focus is a change in cell **mixture**, not in cell **state**. It is not a power failure. | step 16, contrast CT1 |

Two later reports carry the work this one does not: `output/16_summary/step16_FL_comparison.html`
(IB1 vs RB1) and `output/17_summary/step17_PD1_PDL1.html` (the checkpoint question). A glossary
of the biology and statistics is at `output/17_summary/composite_node_lexicon.html`.
</div>

# Objective and assumptions

## The sample and the question

**IB1** is a composite lymph node from a single patient: classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL)
together with follicular lymphoma (FL). **RB1** is the FL recurrence from the same
patient — the same clone, no Hodgkin component. Assayed on the CosMx 6K panel.

The question driving steps 07–12: **can the two disease processes be localised
separately within the composite node, and what distinguishes their microenvironments?**

## Assumptions, and which ones held

```{r assumptions}
a <- data.table(
  Assumption = c(
    "RB1 is a valid negative control for Hodgkin signal",
    "RB1 is a valid negative control PRE-QC",   # RESOLVED in step 16, see revision notice
    "Light-chain restriction identifies the FL clone",
    "Step 07's `B_clean` tier contains B cells",
    "CD30 (TNFRSF8) can identify HRS cells",
    "HRS cells are giant; segmentation may split them",
    "Spatial QC removes damaged tissue, not signal",
    "n = 1 patient — everything is descriptive"),
  Status = c("HELD", "FAILED -> RESOLVED (step 16)", "HELD", "FAILED", "FAILED",
             "TESTED, REJECTED", "HELD, WRONG DIRECTION", "HELD"),
  Evidence = c(
    "RB1 clears no Hodgkin hotspot cut at any threshold",
    "RB1 staining flag is `not_evaluated`; 2.0M IB1-only cells have no counterpart. RESOLVED by step 16's symmetric `matched` tier: 80 hotspots (66 seam-free), zero RB1 bins clear the cut",
    "RB1 is 99% kappa in clustered B cells; IB1 foci reach 0.88",
    "13.4% B cells in the diffuse compartment vs 48.9% clustered",
    "Max 6 counts, 78% singletons; held-out cHL-programme AUC 0.552; RB1 (no Hodgkin) 6.27% CD30+ vs IB1 7.01%. (Revised: the original also cited depth AUC 0.716, which is generic and withdrawn -- see sec. 5.2)",
    "Adjacency 1.03x over a density-matched null, identical in both samples",
    "Discarded cells carry MORE chemokine, not less: +1.20x after correcting for flattening (sec. 4)",
    "Stated in step 01; no inference here is population-level"))
tbl(a, "Assumptions carried into the analysis and how each fared.")
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**Two assumptions failed in ways that changed the analysis.** Step 07's `B_clean` tier
is defined purely by exclusion — light-chain-high, not plasma, not near plasma — and
never tests for B identity, which invalidated the first version of step 08. And CD30
has too little dynamic range on this panel to call HRS cells at all, which redirected
step 10 into step 11.
</div>

## Units and a naming caution

<details>
<summary>`cp10k` means two different things across these scripts — read before comparing numbers</summary>

| where | formula | unit |
|---|---|---|
| step 11 bins | `sum(marker counts) / sum(nCount)` pooled over the bin | share of the **bin's** transcriptome |
| step 10 per-gene | per-cell `marker/nCount`, then averaged over cells | mean of **per-cell** shares |
| myeloid readout A | pooled, as step 11 | bin share |
| myeloid readout B | per-cell, then averaged | mean per-cell share |

The pooled form is depth-weighted, so a few deep cells can carry a bin; the per-cell
mean weights every cell equally. Both were run wherever the distinction could matter
(the DC result below), and they agreed. **Step 10's "CCL17 8.56 vs 1.96" and step 11's
"median bin 4.0" are therefore not directly comparable numbers.**
</details>

## Cell-type labels are audited, not taken from HierAnnot

```{r relabel}
rl <- rd("output/09b_marker_relabel/IB1/cluster_labels_final.csv")
if (!is.null(rl)) {
  x <- rl[clustering == "pearson_clusters_low",
          .(cluster = cluster_id, `% of node` = pct_cells, `% cluster i` = pct_defect,
            label, status, top_z, `HierAnnot said` = hierannot_immune_core,
            agrees)][order(cluster)]
  tbl(x, "Step 09b marker audit of pearson_clusters_low. `top_z` is the family score; higher is stronger. HierAnnot disagrees on 5 of 9.")
}
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**HierAnnot's `annot_path` is wrong on a substantial minority of clusters, in ways that
would invert an interpretation.** Cluster 2 is the follicular stromal/FDC scaffold —
`PDGFRB`, `COL1A1`, `ACTA2` structurally, plus `CLU`, `CR2`, `VCAM1`, `C3`, `CXCL13`
inside follicles — and HierAnnot calls it macrophage. Cluster 5 is endothelium called
neutrophil; cluster 6 is pDC called plasma cell. Choosing a better-scoring hierarchy does
not rescue this: `tme_core` and `tonsil_tme` both outrank `immune_core` on HierAnnot's own
`fit_rank_score`, and both call the dominant cluster "Epithelial > Luminal epithelial" in
a lymph node.

`scripts/09b_script_marker_relabel.R` scores every cluster against a 16-family lymph-node
panel, z-scoring each gene **across clusters** first so no single abundant marker can
carry a call, and attaches a status to each result. It is an audit, not an oracle — it
replaces one automated call with another. What it adds is that a weak call announces
itself: an abundance cap rejects lineages that cannot plausibly be that common, a
child-vs-parent tie resolves to the parent, and `defect_dominated` marks any cluster more
than half over-fixation cells.

**Cluster 0 is that last case, and it is not a cell type.** It is 70% `inSitu_clusters ==
"i"` and holds **86% of every defect cell in IB1**. Its clean 30% remnant scores only
1.04, so it carries no lineage label. Note the consequence for clustering choice: the low
clustering concentrates the defect in one cluster, while `pearson_clusters_high` spreads
it across six (78%, 63%, 61%, 58%, 52%, 52%).
</div>

Downstream scripts read these through `scripts/lib/cluster_labels.R`, which errors rather
than falling back if the audit has not been run for a sample.

# Linear analysis

## Light-chain neighbourhoods (step 07)

Light-chain neighbourhoods are built from two genes only — `IGKC` and `IGLC1/2` — on
cells with ≥4 light-chain counts, after removing plasma cells and their 15 µm spillover
halo, then clustered into spatial graph communities at four radii.

```{r nb-table}
nb <- rd("output/07_lightchain/IB1/lightchain_neighborhoods_r40um.csv")
if (!is.null(nb)) {
  s <- nb[artifact_suspect == FALSE, .(neighbourhoods = .N,
          median_cells = as.numeric(median(n_cells)),
          median_kappa_frac = round(median(kappa_frac), 3)), by = class][order(-neighbourhoods)]
  tbl(s, "IB1 light-chain neighbourhoods at r40um, artifact-suspect excluded. Polytypic ~0.62 is the reactive expectation.")
}
```

```{r nb-global, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Step 07 global view. Panel 3 colours each neighbourhood by aggregate log2 kappa:lambda; red is kappa-restricted (high ratio), blue is lambda-skewed."}
img("output/07_lightchain_global/IB1/IB1_global_r40um.png")
```

### What is actually inside a neighbourhood (step 14)

Steps 07–08 described neighbourhoods by their *called* cells. Step 14 characterises **all
cells occupying the same tissue**, against control regions matched on cell count *and*
median depth, with the **region as the unit of analysis** (68 neighbourhoods vs 204
controls) rather than the cell.

```{r inout-prev}
pv <- rd("output/14_lightchain_in_out/IB1/cluster_prevalence_in_out.csv")
if (!is.null(pv)) {
  x <- pv[clustering == "pearson_clusters_low" & members_dropped == TRUE,
          .(cluster = cluster_id, label, `% in` = round(pct_in,2), `% out` = round(pct_out,2),
            log2_enrichment = round(log2_enr,2))][order(-log2_enrichment)]
  tbl(x, "Cluster prevalence inside vs outside neighbourhood footprints, with the 14,641 CALLED member cells REMOVED. Descriptive log2 enrichment, region as the unit (68 neighbourhoods vs 204 count- and depth-matched controls) -- no per-cluster test, so read the size. Without the member removal the B/plasma rows would restate the selection rule.")
}
```

```{r inout-markers, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Marker expression by cluster, in vs out. Called members removed; IGKC/IGLC shown for reference only as the selection variable."}
img("output/14_lightchain_in_out/IB1/figures/fig_14_heatmap_markers.png")
```

```{r inout-de, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Genes differing in vs out, region as the unit, restricted to genes where cp10k and detection rate agree."}
img("output/14_lightchain_in_out/IB1/figures/fig_14_heatmap_differential.png")
```

<div class="verdict-ok">
**Two coherent programmes, neither of them the selection variable.** Cluster 2 — the
stromal/FDC cluster HierAnnot called macrophage — carries the full follicular scaffold
inside neighbourhoods, concordant in *both* cp10k and detection rate: `CLU` 58.1 vs 10.1
cp10k (69% vs 26% of cells), `VCAM1`, `C3`, `CXCL13`, `CR2`, `CR1`, `SERPINE2`, `FCER2`,
`CCL21`. Cluster 3 carries a Tfh programme: `CXCL13` +2.70, `PDCD1` +0.59, `ICOS` +0.43,
`CTLA4` +0.46 log2.

The Tfh result deserves a note, because **an earlier Tfh claim in this project was
retracted for pseudo-replication** (section 3). This one is not that claim: the unit is
the region, the controls are depth-matched, and the effect is concordant across two
independent measures.
</div>

<div class="verdict-no">
**Neighbourhoods are *less* internally consistent than random tissue**, not more — median
Bray-Curtis distance to the group centroid 0.185 vs 0.128 for matched controls
(p = 3.1e-09). They are not a uniform tissue type. Four are compositional outliers, led by
a lambda-skewed one at 0.505. Composition did **not** separate kappa-restricted FL-like
neighbourhoods from polytypic reactive ones (all q > 0.47) — but only **6 of 17** FL-like
neighbourhoods survive to be tested, so that is underpowered, not negative.
</div>

<details>
<summary>Why 154 neighbourhoods become 68, and whether the loss is biased</summary>

Step 07 built neighbourhoods on the **pre-QC** object (2.54M cells); `pearson_clusters_*`
exist only **post-QC** (400k). The spatial filter removes 84% of IB1, so 86 neighbourhoods
lack enough surviving tissue to characterise.

```{r inout-attrition}
at <- rd("output/14_lightchain_in_out/IB1/neighborhood_attrition.csv")
if (!is.null(at)) tbl(at, "Neighbourhood retention by step-07 class. The p-values below it are Mann-Whitney U on neighbourhood-level summaries (size, cluster-`i` fraction, kappa fraction), one observation per neighbourhood.")
```

Retention is driven by **size** (median 79 cells kept vs 30.5 lost, p = 4.3e-06) and by
**over-fixation burden** (median cluster-`i` fraction 1.8–9.8% kept vs 19.2–33.3% lost).
It is **not** driven by light chain: median `kappa_frac` is 0.754 in retained
neighbourhoods against 0.750 in lost ones, so the FL clone is not being preferentially
discarded.
</details>

<details>
<summary>A normalisation artifact that had to be removed first</summary>

The first pass returned `PHKG2`, `A1BG`, `DUSP2` and `OXR1` as depressed inside
neighbourhoods in **all nine clusters** at roughly 2×, with q down to 1e-20. They are the
highest-abundance genes on the panel (91–114 cp10k), and their **detection rates had moved
only 0.87–0.96×**. cp10k sums to 10,000, so the genuine rise in `CXCL13`/`CLU`/`CD79A`
forces an apparent fall in whatever is most abundant. Negative probes differed only 1.16×
between the groups, so ambient background did not explain it either — the arithmetic did.

Every result above is therefore gated on cp10k and detection rate agreeing in direction
(811 of 953 significant results survive), and figure genes are ranked by the **detection**
effect, which cannot be pushed around by what other genes are doing.
</details>

### RB1 cannot be analysed this way, and that is the finding

Running the same analysis on RB1 stops immediately: **1,276,791 of its 1,286,223 cells sit
inside a light-chain neighbourhood, leaving 689 outside.** In the FL recurrence the
light-chain-restricted compartment *is* the node, so no control tissue exists within the
sample and the in/out contrast is undefined. That is the sharpest available statement of
how the two samples differ: in IB1 the same construction covers a minority of tissue and
leaves real control territory.

## The Hodgkin chemokine field (step 11)

### Why chemokines, and how they were found

Step 10 scored a 21-gene cHL programme with equal weights and z-scored **within sample**.
Both choices were wrong for this question: equal weighting diluted the informative genes,
and within-sample z-scoring makes a between-sample comparison impossible by construction.
Re-examining the genes individually on a common depth-standardised scale found the signal.

```{r chl-genes, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5.2, fig.cap="Only a few of the 21 scored genes carry Hodgkin-specific signal. The rest diluted it."}
g <- rd("output/10_hrs/chl_program_per_gene.csv")
if (!is.null(g)) {
  g[, lab := fifelse(gene %in% c("CCL17","CCL22","BATF3","CD40"), "Hodgkin-specific",
             fifelse(gene == "TNFRSF8", "CD30 (validator)", "flat"))]
  ggplot(g, aes(reorder(gene, ratio_IB1_RB1), ratio_IB1_RB1, fill = lab)) +
    geom_col(width=.72) + coord_flip() +
    geom_hline(yintercept=1, colour=INK, linetype="22", linewidth=.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=c(`Hodgkin-specific`=BLUE, `CD30 (validator)`=ORANGE, flat=MUTED),
                      name=NULL) +
    labs(title="IB1 : RB1 per gene, depth-standardised",
         subtitle="Counts per 10k on a common scale. 1.0 = no difference between the composite node and the FL recurrence.",
         x=NULL, y="IB1 : RB1 ratio",
         caption="Data: output/10_hrs/chl_program_per_gene.csv") + th
}
```

```{r chl-tab}
if (!is.null(g)) tbl(head(g[order(-ratio_IB1_RB1), .(gene, cp10k_IB1, cp10k_RB1,
     pct_det_IB1, pct_det_RB1, ratio_IB1_RB1)], 8),
     "Top genes by IB1:RB1 ratio. CCL17/TARC and CCL22/MDC are the canonical HRS chemokines; serum TARC is a clinical cHL biomarker.")
```

### Is it composition rather than biology?

RB1's node is effaced by FL (39.9% B cells vs IB1's 8.5%), so "IB1 has more T/DC-zone
chemokine" was a live alternative. It is refuted: the elevation holds **within every
lineage**, and composition standardisation *raises* the ratio rather than lowering it.

```{r confound}
cf <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/niche_confound_within_lineage.csv")
if (!is.null(cf)) tbl(cf[order(-ratio)], "CCL17+CCL22 per cell within each lineage, depth-standardised. No lineage is near 1.")
st <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/niche_confound_standardised.csv")
if (!is.null(st)) tbl(st, "Whole-sample ratio raw vs standardised to each sample's cell mix. Composition was diluting the signal, not creating it.")
```

### Field versus hotspots

Two thresholds answer two questions. RB1's 99th percentile asks *is IB1 elevated at
all* — so pervasively that ~27% of bins clear it, which is a **field** rather than
a niche. (Revision 2026-09-01: "tissue-wide" in the original overstated the extent. Step 17
measured it — the elevation decays **2.71× [1.95, 3.91]** from 100–400 µm to >1600 µm from a
hotspot against **1.20×** in RB1, so most of the field is spent by **400–800 µm**. A flat
**4.07×** IB1:RB1 residual persists beyond that which is *not* a decaying field and remains
unattributed. See `field_extent_verdict.csv`.) IB1's own 99th percentile isolates the **focal hotspots**.

```{r sweep, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.4, fig.cap="Seam-free hotspots are a stable core; total hotspots simply track the shrinking bin pool."}
sw <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/niche_min_cells_sweep.csv")
if (!is.null(sw)) {
  m <- melt(sw[, .(min_cells, hotspots, hotspots_seam_free)], id.vars="min_cells")
  ggplot(m, aes(min_cells, value, colour=variable)) +
    geom_line(linewidth=.8) + geom_point(size=2.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values=c(hotspots=MUTED, hotspots_seam_free=BLUE), name=NULL) +
    labs(title="MIN_CELLS sweep, post-QC",
         subtitle="RB1 clears the cut at zero bins for every value tested.",
         x="minimum cells per 100 um bin", y="hotspots",
         caption="Data: output/11_hodgkin_niche/niche_min_cells_sweep.csv") + th
}
if (!is.null(sw)) tbl(sw, "The seam-free count is flat across thresholds; the total is not.")
```

```{r niche-global, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Step 11 global, post-QC. Panel 2: hotspots (dark, blue outline = seam-free, amber = seam-flagged) on the elevated field. Panel 3: the continuous score."}
img("output/11_hodgkin_niche_global/IB1_global_bin100um_postqc.png")
```

### Pre-QC: the map versus the control

The spatial QC keeps 15.8% of IB1 and leaves **613 of 758 FOVs with zero passing
cells**. The filter does not enrich for the signal — discarded cells carry *more*
chemokine than kept ones (section 4) — so the post-QC estimate is conservative and
mapping pre-QC is defensible for *position*. Pre-QC *magnitudes* are not, and the RB1
control cannot follow either, because RB1's staining flag is `not_evaluated`.

```{r preqc}
pc <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/preqc_bin_coverage.csv")
if (!is.null(pc)) tbl(pc[, .(bins=.N, med_cells=as.numeric(median(cells)),
     med_cp10k=round(median(chemo_cp10k),1), q99=round(quantile(chemo_cp10k,.99),1),
     max=round(max(chemo_cp10k))), by=set], "Bin coverage, pre-QC vs post-QC.")
ov <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/preqc_hotspot_overlap.csv")
if (!is.null(ov)) tbl(ov, "Hotspot overlap. 175 of 180 pre-QC hotspots sit in territory that has no bin post-QC.")
```

```{r preqc-global, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Step 11 global, pre-QC. Both tissue pieces are fully tiled; the post-QC version leaves large regions blank."}
img("output/11_hodgkin_niche_global/IB1_global_bin100um_preqc.png")
```

## Differential genes and neighbouring cell changes

### What is in a hotspot

```{r comp}
cp <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/niche_composition.csv")
if (!is.null(cp)) tbl(cp, "Bin composition. f_* are percentages of neighbours within 30 um; med_area in um2.")
sec <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/niche_secondary_markers.csv")
if (!is.null(sec)) tbl(sec, "Secondary markers, none of which define the niche — independent corroboration.")
```

### The macrophage anomaly, and its resolution

Hotspots looked macrophage-**depleted**, which contradicts the tumour-associated
macrophage picture in cHL. Testing both averaging schemes and the called cell types
resolves it: these are **dendritic-cell** regions.

```{r myeloid, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Mature DC (LAMP3/CCR7) and cDC1 up; macrophage markers down. Both weightings agree."}
my <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/hotspot_myeloid_marker_sets.csv")
if (!is.null(my)) {
  w <- dcast(my, set ~ readout, value.var="ratio")
  setnames(w, 2:3, c("A_pooled","B_percell"))
  m <- melt(w, id.vars="set", variable.name="readout", value.name="ratio")
  ggplot(m, aes(reorder(set, ratio), ratio, fill=readout)) +
    geom_col(position=position_dodge(.8), width=.74) + coord_flip() +
    geom_hline(yintercept=1, colour=INK, linetype="22", linewidth=.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=c(A_pooled=BLUE, B_percell=AQUA), name=NULL) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    labs(title="Hotspot : background, by marker set",
         subtitle="A = pooled bin share (depth-weighted); B = mean of per-cell shares. Log scale.",
         x=NULL, y="hotspot : background ratio",
         caption="Data: output/11_hodgkin_niche/hotspot_myeloid_marker_sets.csv") + th
}
```

```{r myeloid-lin}
ln <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/hotspot_myeloid_lineage.csv")
if (!is.null(ln)) {
  lw <- dcast(ln, lineage ~ grp, value.var="pct")
  if (all(c("hotspot","background") %in% names(lw))) {
    lw[, ratio := round(hotspot/pmax(background,1e-9),2)]
    tbl(lw[order(-hotspot)], "Called lineage composition (%). Step 01's myeloid set is macrophage-weighted and contains no DC-specific gene, so DC-rich regions fall into ambiguous / all_markers_0.")
  }
}
wm <- rd("output/11_hodgkin_niche/hotspot_myeloid_within_myeloid.csv")
if (!is.null(wm)) tbl(wm[order(-ratio)], "Within called-myeloid cells only. The chemokine row is CIRCULAR (bins were called on chemokine) and must not be quoted as evidence; the DC and macrophage rows are not.")
```

<div class="verdict-ok">
**Resolution.** CCL17/CCL22 are the signature secretions of mature/migratory LAMP3⁺CCR7⁺
dendritic cells, not only of HRS cells. The hotspots are DC territory: cDC1 1.83×, mature
DC 1.59×, macrophage 0.77×, `mac_core` 0.57× — consistent across both weightings, and
mirrored in the called lineages. Caveat: LAMP3/CCR7 rising where CCL17/CCL22 rises is
close to definitional, so it identifies the **cellular source** rather than proving
something independent. The macrophage depletion and the within-myeloid phenotype shift
*are* independent.
</div>

# Dead ends and negative results

Four substantial lines of work returned negatives. Each is reported because the negative
constrains what the data can support — and in two cases the failure produced the method
that worked.

## Clustered vs diffuse B cells failed its own control (step 08a)

```{r s08}
p <- rd("output/08_ib1_hierannot_bcells/marker_panel_scores.csv")
if (!is.null(p)) {
  w <- dcast(p[group != "diffuse"], panel + group ~ set, value.var="ratio")
  tbl(w[order(panel, group)], "Panel score relative to diffuse -- descriptive ratios, no test. The point is the IDENTITY CONTROL: a contrast that cannot recover a B-cell panel in its own B cells has failed before any p-value is relevant. 'step-07 pool' is the failing version; 'HierAnnot B' is the same contrast on a positive B-cell definition.")
}
```

<div class="verdict-no">
The `BCELL` identity control came back at **2.86×** and `PC` at **0.63×** — the diffuse
compartment was not the same cell type as the clustered one. Cause: step 07's `B_clean`
tier is defined by exclusion and never tests B identity; the diffuse compartment is
**13.4% B cells** against 48.9% clustered. Everything contrasted against it was
uninterpretable.
</div>

**What it produced.** A cluster-level B-cell call (step 09, HierAnnot on
`pearson_clusters_low`, 31,651 cells at a 4.2× marker margin), and a redone step 08 that
passes both gates — `BCELL` 1.14, `PC` 1.00. On that footing the answer is a clean
negative: FL-like foci are **not** transcriptionally distinguishable from other clustered
B-cell neighbourhoods (all q ≥ 0.68; BCL2-within-GC 20.5% vs 23.4%).

<div class="verdict-mid">
**Revision 2026-09-01 — the verdict holds and the reason is better than stated here.** This
section reads the null as a limit of power at n = 6 foci. Step 16 repeated the comparison
*conditioned on cell type* and found **zero significant genes within B cells or within T
cells**. So the FL focus is a change in the **mixture** of cells present, not in how any cell
type behaves — a positive structural finding, not a failure to detect one. Step 16 contrast
CT1.
</div>

## HRS cells cannot be called from this panel (step 10)

```{r s10}
s <- rd("output/10_hrs/summary.csv")
if (!is.null(s)) tbl(s, "Step 10 summary. The held-out CD30 AUC of 0.55 is the gate that fails.")
```

```{r cd30-dist, fig.width=7, fig.height=4, fig.cap="CD30 has almost no dynamic range: 78% of positive cells carry a single transcript."}
seg <- rd("output/10_hrs/hrs_segments.csv.gz", select=c("samp","cd30_ct"))
if (!is.null(seg)) {
  d <- seg[samp=="IB1", .N, by=.(cd30 = pmin(cd30_ct, 6L))][order(cd30)]
  ggplot(d, aes(factor(cd30), N)) + geom_col(fill=ORANGE, width=.7) +
    scale_y_log10() +
    labs(title="TNFRSF8 (CD30) counts per cell, IB1", subtitle="log scale; max observed is 6 counts",
         x="CD30 counts", y="cells", caption="Data: output/10_hrs/hrs_segments.csv.gz") + th
}
```

<div class="verdict-no">
CD30 tops out at 6 counts with 78% singletons; the 21-gene cHL programme *anti*-tracks CD30
(AUC 0.46, held-out 0.552 — the gate that fails); and **RB1, which has no Hodgkin, is 6.27%
CD30⁺ against IB1's 7.01%**. Rendered top-scoring objects are ordinary lymphocytes
indistinguishable from RB1 controls. Any one of the last three closes the question; the RB1
comparison alone is decisive, since near-identical CD30⁺ fractions in a sample without Hodgkin
mean CD30 is not marking Hodgkin here.
</div>

<div class="verdict-mid">
**One leg of this argument is withdrawn (revision 2026-09-01), and the conclusion is
unaffected.** The original version also cited "sequencing depth alone predicts CD30 positivity
at **AUC 0.716**". Step 16 later calibrated that statistic against genes whose presence is not
in doubt and found **AUC 0.64–0.76 against depth for every sparse gene on this panel** —
*IGKC* 0.693 (the transcript the FL clone is defined by), *CD3E* 0.695, *CD68* 0.731. CD30's
0.716 is indistinguishable from those, so it says nothing about CD30 specifically: it is a
property of thresholding sparse counts on this platform.

The transferable lesson, which is why this is annotated rather than deleted: **a depth-vs-
positivity AUC near 0.70 is not evidence that a sparse gene is noise.** Calibrate it against a
gene you are certain of before using it to reject one you are not.
</div>

## Segmentation fragmentation was tested and rejected

The hypothesis: HRS cells are giant, so segmentation splits them into normal-sized
fragments, which would explain why called cells were only 1.6× background area.

```{r merge-null}
mn <- rd("output/10_hrs/hrs_merge_null.csv")
if (!is.null(mn)) tbl(mn, "Adjacent CD30+ segments merged into connected components, against a density-matched permutation null.")
```

<div class="verdict-no">
Adjacency runs **1.03× over the null in IB1 and 1.03× in RB1** — identical. Merging also
made morphology *worse* (object area 1.76× background vs 1.99× per segment). The same
code returns 2.21× (p = 0.030) on synthetic data where fragmentation is real, so this is
a measurement rather than a failure to look.
</div>

## Results that did not survive their own scrutiny

```{r retractions}
r <- data.table(
  Claim = c("Hodgkin niche avoids the FL foci",
            "The diffuse compartment is residual plasma",
            "Tfh programme differs around FL-like foci",
            "Merging beats its null (p = 0.0495)",
            "Hotspots sit on FOV seams"),
  `First reported` = c("997 vs 681 um, p = 9.7e-21", "PC markers 1.5x elevated",
                       "p = 1.66e-14", "1.03x, p < 0.05", "median 33.7 vs 41.0 um, p = 0.045"),
  `On re-examination` = c("798 vs 757 um, p = 0.686; then p = 0.233 / 0.19 in step 12",
                          "2.3x enriched but a minority; the real issue is 86.6% non-B",
                          "p = 0.048 at the neighbourhood level, q = 0.53",
                          "3% excess; significant only because n ~ 15,000",
                          "real but modest; signal survives excluding all seam bins"),
  Cause = c("threshold covering 29% of tissue compared regions, not niches",
            "over-reading a secondary effect", "pseudo-replication over 6 neighbourhoods",
            "p-value without an effect size", "flag caught ~half the tissue by geometry"))
tbl(r, "Claims made and then corrected during the analysis.")
```

<details>
<summary>Seam artifact: the check that the original FOV test could not do</summary>

Step 11's FOV check asks whether hotspots concentrate in *particular* FOVs — they do not
(25 FOVs, 1.4 bins each, FOV identity explains 31% of variance). But seams occur in
**every** FOV, so that test is blind to them. A direct distance-to-seam test found
hotspots modestly seam-biased (median 33.7 vs 41.0 µm, p = 0.045), with cells and
transcript totals halving within 25 µm. The decisive control: dropping every bin within
75 µm of a seam leaves IB1's q99 at 111.5 cp10k with **zero RB1 bins reaching it**.
`SEAM_UM` was tightened from 50 µm (which flagged ~half the tissue by geometry) to 25 µm.
</details>

## What the negatives constrain

<div class="verdict-mid">
1. **No per-cell HRS identification** from this panel, with or without more data —
   the limit is CD30's dynamic range, not the calling method.
2. **No transcriptional signature separating FL-like foci** from other clustered B-cell
   neighbourhoods at 6K depth. (Revision 2026-09-01: originally attributed to n = 6 foci.
   Step 16 shows it is not a power limit — zero genes differ *within* B or T cells, so the
   focus is a change in cell mixture, not cell state.)
3. **No spatial relationship between the two diseases** in this node.
4. **What does work** is regional: a Hodgkin chemokine field, lineage-independent and
   decaying over **400–800 µm** (2.71× vs RB1's 1.20×; revision 2026-09-01, originally
   described as "tissue-wide"), with focal DC-rich hotspots that have no RB1 equivalent.
</div>

# Over-fixation in IB1

Everything above excludes InSituType cluster `i` before doing anything else. That
exclusion is not housekeeping — it rests on a formal diagnosis
(`scripts/sbatch/qc_ib1_overfixation_summary.R`,
`output/07_overfixation/ib1_overfixation_summary.md`) whose conclusions constrain how
IB1 may be analysed at all. This section summarises it and connects it forward.

<div class="verdict-ok">
**Verdict: SUPPORTED.** 9 of 9 mechanism criteria fired; every competing hypothesis is
eliminated. Cluster `i` is **37.1% of IB1** against **8.1% of RB1** — a 4.6× dose
difference, spatially organised in IB1 and not in RB1.
</div>

## Two claims that must not be merged

**(A) Cluster `i` inside IB1 is a technical defect population.** This is what the
criteria test, and where the over-fixation call lives.

**(B) IB1 as a whole is degraded relative to RB1.** **Not asserted, and not testable
this way.** At matched depth IB1's B markers fall (MS4A1 0.17×, CD79A 0.43×) while its
myeloid and stromal markers *rise* (LYZ 2.81×, COL1A1 2.22×) — the signature of
different tissue composition, not uniform probe occlusion. Composition and fixation are
entangled across blocks, so the cross-sample contrast is reported and set aside.

## The argument in one paragraph

The lesion is **qualitative, not quantitative**. Defect cells are not shallow — they
carry **1.11× the counts** of their neighbours at **1.03× the area**. What they have lost
is the ability to say anything: no gene is enriched in them (max log2FC **0.98** against
**3.73** for other clusters). Against IB1's own unaffected cells at matched depth, the
profile is dragged toward uniform — detection ratio falls with a gene's baseline
prevalence at slope **−0.30** (p = 0.00096). Common genes lose, rare genes gain, which is
what a flat background floor does to a compositional measure and is *not* how a cell type
behaves. Measured directly: at equal library size (547 vs 560 counts) defect cells commit
**0.61%** of their budget to the 22-gene marker panel against **1.55%** for matched
neighbours — a ratio of **0.39**.

Degradation would remove molecules and show up as fewer counts, fewer features and a
rising negative-probe share. None is present. Crosslinking removes **access**, not
material — the transcripts are there but unavailable, and counting continues on
background.

```{r overfix-overview, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Over-fixation diagnostic overview: all nine criteria."}
img("output/07_overfixation/figures/overfixation_overview.png")
```

## The three load-bearing observations

```{r overfix-evidence}
ev <- data.table(
  Observation = c("Protein channels split (C1)", "Protein and RNA co-vary (C8)",
                  "Diffusion-shaped gradient (C7)"),
  Finding = c("Membrane 0.75x, CD45 0.79x, but DAPI **rises** to 1.32x",
              "Across 758 FOVs, rho -0.58 with Membrane, +0.26 with DAPI",
              "Defect fraction climbs 12.3% -> 60.6% core to rim (rho 0.34); RB1 flat (rho -0.05)"),
  `Why it matters` = c(
    "Exactly the split expected when formaldehyde masks protein epitopes but leaves the DNA minor groove open. Localises the insult to the fixative, not the antibodies.",
    "Two independent accidents would not co-vary field by field.",
    "Formalin diffuses inward from the block surface, so over-fixation is rim-worst. Global radius outranks local boundary distance (rho -0.12) — a block-scale cause, not a section-handling artifact."))
tbl(ev, "The observations that carry the diagnosis.")
```

```{r overfix-c1c7, out.width="49%", fig.show="hold", fig.cap="Left: protein-channel dissociation (C1) — antibody channels fall while DAPI rises. Right: the radial gradient (C7) — rim-worst in IB1, flat in RB1."}
img("output/07_overfixation/figures/C1_channel_dissociation.png")
img("output/07_overfixation/figures/C7_radial_gradient.png")
```

## The gradient, and what salvage costs

```{r overfix-radial}
rg <- rd("output/07_overfixation/ib1_overfixation_radial_gradient.csv")
if (!is.null(rg)) tbl(rg[, .(sample = merge_sample, radial_quintile = rq, n,
                             median_r, pct_defect, median_nCount, pct_strongB)],
  "Defect fraction by radial quintile, core (1) to rim (5). IB1 climbs; RB1 does not.")
sv <- rd("output/07_overfixation/ib1_overfixation_salvage.csv")
if (!is.null(sv)) tbl(dcast(sv, filter ~ merge_sample, value.var = c("pct_kept","pct_strongB")),
  "Salvage options. `pct_strongB` is the yield of confidently-called B cells — the quality gained per cell discarded.")

## How this constrains steps 07–12

```{r overfix-link}
lk <- data.table(
  `Over-fixation finding` = c(
    "Cluster `i` is a technical defect, 37.1% of IB1",
    "Detection-rate comparisons across samples are confounded",
    "The defect is a continuum; cluster `i` is a thresholded readout",
    "Flattening makes common genes lose and RARE genes gain",
    "Only 145 of 758 IB1 FOVs survive spatial QC"),
  `Consequence downstream` = c(
    "Excluded before scoring in steps 08b, 10, 11, 12 — reported, never silent",
    "Every cross-sample number here is depth-standardised across pooled deciles, exactly as the salvage note requires",
    "Dropping cluster `i` leaves a graded residue, so residual defect is a live confound in every IB1 number",
    "CCL17 is a HIGH-prevalence gene (95th percentile of the panel), so flattening DEPRESSES it in defect cells",
    "Drove the pre-QC map (step 11), which recovers 613 otherwise-dark FOVs"))
tbl(lk, "The diagnosis is upstream of every result in this report.")
```

<div class="verdict-mid">
**Tested, and it inverts the earlier reading.** The pre-QC check found CCL17+CCL22 at
10.27 cp10k in `dim_membrane` cells against 9.98 in `ok` cells, and that near-parity
(0.97×) was read as "the filter does not select the signal". A point estimate cannot
carry that claim: it has no equivalence bound, and C2's flattening gives every gene an
*expected* ratio, so a raw value near 1 could be a real effect cancelled by flattening.

`scripts/sbatch/qc_11_flattening_vs_chemokine.R` regresses log2(detection ratio) on
log2(baseline prevalence) across all 6,175 genes in 120,000 depth-matched IB1 cells, then
locates the chemokines against the fit. Two things came out, and the first corrects an
error in an earlier draft of this section: **CCL17 sits at the 95th prevalence percentile**,
not the low end, so flattening *depresses* it — the opposite of what was assumed. And
after that correction the chemokines are **enriched in the discarded cells by 1.20×
(CCL17, +1.83 SD) and 1.18× (CCL22, +1.62 SD)**, while `CD68` (0.83×), `CD3E` (0.90×) and
`MS4A1` (0.91×) go the other way — a specific contrast, not a global shift.

*Consequence.* The QC filter is discarding chemokine-rich cells, so **the post-QC step-11
estimate is conservative** and the headline IB1:RB1 contrast is not inflated by selection.
But pre-QC expansion is no longer a free coverage gain: the 2.0M added cells carry a
chemokine excess of unresolved origin. Note that their *detection rate* is up 13–18% while
*abundance* is up only 3% — the signature of the same transcripts spread across more cells
by poor segmentation, rather than more transcripts. **Pre-QC hotspot positions stand;
pre-QC magnitudes should be read as upper bounds.**
</div>

<details>
<summary>What the over-fixation analysis explicitly cannot settle</summary>

- **Fixation time is not measured.** The data show a crosslinking-shaped lesion with a
  surface-in gradient; they cannot separate prolonged formalin from a failed
  antigen-retrieval or protease step. The block's processing record is outside this dataset.
- **H7 (section handling) is disfavoured, not formally excluded** — global radius beats
  local edge distance, but both are 2-D projections of a 3-D gradient.
- **Claim (B) is untested, not disproved.** Whether IB1 as a whole is mildly over-fixed
  needs a within-IB1 dose axis or a second control block of the same tissue type.
- **Cluster `i` is not unique to IB1** — it is 8.1% of RB1 and flattens there too. The
  diagnosis is about *dose* and spatial organisation, not about the mode existing.
- **C9 rests on its marker-share term** (0.39×). Its entropy term moves the right way but
  only slightly (310 vs 306 effective genes) and should not be quoted alone.
- **CD45 is a leukocyte marker as well as a channel**, so its fall is not independent of
  composition. C1 rests on the *split* between antibody channels and DAPI, which no
  compositional change produces on its own.
- **Cluster `i` was fit on this data**, so within-sample contrasts compare a data-derived
  group against its own complement. RB1 is the guard: same definition, same flattening,
  yet 4–5× rarer with no radial gradient and no channel coupling.
</details>

                         "Inputs unavailable when this report was rendered; the corresponding blocks are omitted above.")
```

<details>
<summary>Known caveats carried forward</summary>

- **n = 1 patient.** Every result is descriptive and hypothesis-generating.
- **CCL17/CCL22 are secreted**, so a hotspot marks where chemokine signalling is
  happening, not which cell produces it.
- **Pre-QC positions are more trustworthy than pre-QC magnitudes** — those cells failed
  QC for reasons beyond chemokine content.
- **The RB1 control is post-QC only.** Any pre-QC specificity claim is unsupported.
- **`SEAM_UM` and `MIN_CELLS` are choices**, both swept and reported; the seam-free
  hotspot core (~12–18 post-QC) is what is stable across them.
- **cp10k is compositional.** A genuine rise in some genes forces an apparent fall in the
  panel's most abundant ones. Step 14 gates every call on detection rate agreeing; earlier
  steps reporting cp10k alone have not been re-audited for this.
- **Step 14 characterises 68 of 154 neighbourhoods** — the rest lack post-QC tissue. The
  loss tracks size and defect burden, not light chain, but only 6 FL-like neighbourhoods
  survive, so FL-vs-reactive comparisons there are underpowered rather than negative.
- **Cluster labels are a marker audit, not ground truth** (step 09b). Statuses
  `weak_support`, `ambiguous` and `defect_dominated` mark where the call is soft.
</details>
